changes.before: Build the two required choices with unique labels and the Early visit default. Keep both name attributes equal to slot. The local data check reads the default; manually test keyboard radio movement and a required empty group in a real browser.
changes.after: Let someone choose one visit time from a pair of radio buttons.

before: A radio group offers mutually exclusive choices. Sharing a name within the same form permits at most one selected radio; it does not force an initial selection. required adds the validation requirement that the group have a selection.

type="radio" chooses the control kind. Both inputs use name="slot" to form one group, but unique ids connect their own labels. value chooses the submitted value, not the visible label. checked supplies a default selection. required on a member makes the same-name group required; repeating it on both here keeps that intention clear. fieldset and legend name the overall question.

```html
<form id="visit">
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Choose a visit time</legend>
    <input type="radio" id="early" name="slot" value="early" required checked><label for="early">Early visit</label>
    <input type="radio" id="late" name="slot" value="late" required><label for="late">Late visit</label>
  </fieldset>
  <button type="submit">Request time</button>
</form>
```
Initially the selected early input contributes slot=early. The unchecked late input contributes nothing. Choosing late in a real browser deselects early and changes the submitted pair. Without either checked attribute the page may start with no selection; required does not automatically choose one. Native validation is separate from simply constructing form data.

Build the two required choices with unique labels and the Early visit default. Keep both name attributes equal to slot. The local data check reads the default; manually test keyboard radio movement and a required empty group in a real browser. The supplied checks inspect markup or local form-data relationships; they do not submit a network request or certify a screen-reader or native-browser experience. Optional local practice: try the changed case in a disposable local page and explain the difference.
after: A radio button is a round choice control. Radio buttons with the same `name` in one form belong to one group. Choosing one turns the other off. Use them when someone should choose at most one answer.

Each radio button needs its own `id` and label, but both share a `name`. `value` says what the choice sends. `checked` chooses a starting option. `required` asks the person to choose; it does not choose for them.

This form starts with Early visit selected.

```html
<form id="visit">
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Choose a visit time</legend>
    <input type="radio" id="early" name="slot" value="early" required checked><label for="early">Early visit</label>
    <input type="radio" id="late" name="slot" value="late" required><label for="late">Late visit</label>
  </fieldset>
  <button type="submit">Request time</button>
</form>
```

The fieldset and legend name the question. Both radios use `name="slot"`. The checked radio sends `slot=early`. If someone chooses Late visit, the form sends `slot=late` instead.

Build the shown form inside main. Use form id `visit`, radio ids `early` and `late`, and the shared name `slot`. Add both labels and the legend `Choose a visit time`. Require both radios and start with Early visit checked. Run the checks, then try choosing Late visit.
